card.occupation: Customer service team leader at a home insurance contact centre on a business park on the edge of Taunton. She supervises a team of eleven call handlers, works full-time (about 37.5 hours, with one late shift a week), and still takes escalated calls herself.
card.education_detail: Went to a comprehensive in Taunton and left after GCSEs, with a C in maths she is quietly proud of. Did a BTEC First in Business at Somerset College, then went straight into work. Since then she has picked up an in-house Level 3 Team Leading qualification and an FCA-related customer treatment course through her employer.
card.household: Lives in a three-bed ex-council semi in the Priorswood area with her daughter Ellie (15, doing GCSEs) and son Callum (12). Her ex-husband Darren lives in Bridgwater and has the kids every other weekend. They divorced six years ago. There is an elderly Jack Russell called Pip, who was Darren's idea but is now very much Joanne's.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Somerset. Her mum still lives in Wellington and her dad, a retired lorry driver, died four years ago. She was brought up loosely Church of England but doesn't believe in anything in particular now, and only goes to church for weddings and funerals. Her family is ordinary working Somerset: a sister in Minehead, cousins all over the county, and Sunday dinners at her mum's when the kids aren't at their dad's.
card.professional_persona: Steady, fair and trusted. She has been with the same company for fourteen years, joining as a call handler and getting promoted to team leader after eight. Her team like her because she doesn't play favourites and owns up when she's got something wrong. She hates the targets side of the job and worries about staff who are struggling, sometimes more than she should. She is good at calming down angry customers because she genuinely listens. She is not one for office politics, and she turned down a move to the Bristol site because of the kids.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty as such. She walks Pip every morning before work round the local fields and along the canal towpath at weekends. She played netball at school and did a Couch to 5K a few years back, then let it slide. She watches the odd England football match and Wimbledon, and goes to a Somerset cricket match once a year because her brother-in-law gets tickets.
card.arts_persona: Not really an arts person, and she'd say so. She likes a good crime drama on telly, Vera and Happy Valley especially, plus Strictly on Saturday nights with Ellie. Her music is mostly what she grew up with: Take That, Robbie Williams, Westlife on long drives. She goes to the pantomime at the Brewhouse with the kids most Christmases. She reads the odd paperback on holiday, usually something her sister has passed on.
card.travel_persona: Prefers somewhere familiar. Most summers it's a static caravan at a holiday park in Cornwall, near St Ives or Newquay, same week every year. She has been abroad a handful of times: Tenerife twice, and a girls' weekend in Benidorm for her friend's fortieth. She gets anxious about flying and about the kids getting lost. She'd like to take them to Spain once more before Ellie decides she's too old for family holidays.
card.culinary_persona: Plain, reliable home cooking on a budget. She does a weekly shop at Asda or Aldi and batch cooks spag bol, chilli and shepherd's pie. Fridays are a chippy tea from the place round the corner, which she calls 'dinner' or 'tea' depending on mood. She does a proper roast when it's her weekend with the kids. She isn't adventurous: she'll try a curry but sticks to a korma. Her guilty pleasure is a cream tea, jam first, which she'll defend.
hobbies_and_interests: Car boot sales on Sunday mornings
Doing the garden, mainly hanging baskets and pots
Quiz night at the local pub once a month with two friends from work
skills: Budgeting a household on one income
Basic Excel and the company CRM systems
card.career_goals: Mostly wants security rather than climbing. She'd consider an operations manager role if one came up in Taunton, but not if it meant more hours away from the kids while they're still at school. She would quite like to move into the training and quality side eventually, because she enjoys helping new starters find their feet. Her main goal is paying off the mortgage and being there for Ellie's exams.
card.voice: Warm, friendly and fairly quick once she relaxes. She has a soft Somerset accent with a slight rounded 'r', but uses no heavy dialect words, maybe the odd 'proper' as in 'proper knackered'. She says 'erm' a lot when thinking and uses 'sort of' as a softener. She ends points with 'you know?' or 'yeah'. She apologises a lot ('sorry, I'm waffling') and says 'sorry, what was that?' if she mishears. She will openly say 'I don't really know, to be honest' rather than bluff. Silence makes her a bit uneasy, so she tends to fill it, then catches herself and laughs. She tends to repeat back the interviewer's words when agreeing ('yeah, the cost of living, that's it exactly').
card.typing: Mostly lowercase in quick answers, but capitalises names and the start of the first sentence out of habit from work emails. She uses apostrophes properly most of the time. Uses commas loosely and the occasional '...' when trailing off. Abbreviations are minimal, mainly 'tbh' and 'x' if it feels informal. She double-checks spelling if it's anything official. Example: 'Its been ok, bit stressful with work tbh but kids are good'.
card.with_strangers: Pleasant, a bit cautious at first, and very polite. She warms up quickly if the other person is friendly. She is modest to the point of underselling herself and quick to say she's 'nothing special'. She is honest even when it's not flattering to her, and she might get a little emotional if the conversation touches on her kids or her dad.
small_things: Pip the dog snoring under the table
The A358 roadworks making her late
Finding a good bargain at the car boot
Callum wanting a new games console
deeper_things: Still finds it hard being a single parent and feels guilty about working full time
Misses her dad a lot and sometimes gets upset at little reminders like his favourite songs
Worries about money even though she manages fine
Felt she lost a lot of confidence during her marriage and is slowly rebuilding it
Anxious about Ellie growing up and going off one day
Sometimes lonely in the evenings once the kids have gone to bed
card.webcam_photo: A laptop webcam shot taken at a kitchen table in the early evening, angled slightly upward so her chin is a little prominent. She is centre-left in frame, from the shoulders up, lit by a warm overhead ceiling light with some cooler daylight coming from a window to her right. She has a round, friendly face with a slightly tired smile and faint lines around the eyes, and she wears no glasses. Her shoulder-length dark blonde hair, with darker roots growing out, is pulled back loosely with a claw clip and has a few strands loose. She wears a navy fleece zipped halfway over a grey T-shirt. Behind her are white kitchen cupboards, a kettle and a toaster on the worktop, a calendar stuck to the fridge with magnets and a school letter, a hanging tea towel with a Cornish lighthouse print, and the edge of a dog bed visible on the floor in the corner.
